item.title: ०५७ सुमन्त्रस्य अयोध्यागमनम्
item.description:
वाचनम्
सर्वाष् टीकाः
Murali Krishnamurthy Kopalle Murthy - Intro

Book II : Ayodhya Kanda - Book Of Ayodhya

Sumantra takes leave from Guha, who learns from his spies that Rama departed for Chitrakuta. Sumantra drives back to Ayodhya. Entering the royal gynaeceum, he submits to the emperor what he earlier reported to the citizens who followed his chariot. Dasaratha and Kausalya fall into a faint to hear about Rama’s departure for Chitrakuta. All the inmates of gynaeceum weep loudly in anguish.

भागसूचना
  1. सुमन्त्रका अयोध्याको लौटना, उनके मुखसे श्रीरामका संदेश सुनकर पुरवासियोंका विलाप, राजा दशरथ और कौसल्याकी मूर्च्छा तथा अन्तःपुरकी रानियोंका आर्तनाद

item.title: ०५८ रामसन्देशनिवेदनम्
item.description:
वाचनम्
सर्वाष् टीकाः
Murali Krishnamurthy Kopalle Murthy - Intro

Book II : Ayodhya Kanda - Book Of Ayodhya

As per the orders of king Dasaratha, Sumantra delivers the parting messages of Rama and Lakshmana. Rama sends positive messages to Kausalya and Bharata but Lakshmana sends angry messages to Dasaratha.

भागसूचना
  1. महाराज दशरथकी आज्ञासे सुमन्त्रका श्रीराम और लक्ष्मणके संदेश सुनाना
सर्वाष् टीकाः - अवतारिका
English (Gemini 4, itihasa.io)

Regaining consciousness from his swoon, King Daśaratha—sighing like a newly captured elephant—summons Sumantra and asks in anguish how Rāma, accustomed to royal couches, now sleeps upon the bare earth.

item.title: ०५९ दशरथविलापः
item.description:
वाचनम्
सर्वाष् टीकाः
Murali Krishnamurthy Kopalle Murthy - Intro

Book II : Ayodhya Kanda - Book Of Ayodhya

Sumantra narrates the ghastly fate of Ayodhya, both its animate and inanimate beings. Dasaratha laments and soon falls unconscious.

भागसूचना
  1. सुमन्त्रद्वारा श्रीरामके शोकसे जड-चेतन एवं अयोध्यापुरीकी दुरवस्थाका वर्णन तथा राजा दशरथका विलाप
सर्वाष् टीकाः - अवतारिका
English (Gemini 4, itihasa.io)

Sumantra recounts how his weeping horses refused to move on the return journey, how he lingered with Guha hoping Rāma might summon him back, and how the very trees, rivers, and woods of Kosala have withered in grief for Rāma.

item.title: ०६० सुमन्त्रकृतकौसल्यासान्त्वनम्
item.description:
वाचनम्
सर्वाष् टीकाः
Murali Krishnamurthy Kopalle Murthy - Intro

Book II : Ayodhya Kanda - Book Of Ayodhya

Sumantra was unable to console Kausalya, who lied on the floor due to her extreme grief over her separation from Rama, even though he tries to avert her grief by telling her that Rama can reside in the forest delightfully, by warding off his agony.

भागसूचना
  1. कौसल्याका विलाप और सारथि सुमन्त्रका उन्हें समझाना
सर्वाष् टीकाः - अवतारिका
English (Gemini 4, itihasa.io)

Trembling on the ground like one possessed, Kausalyā begs Sumantra to drive her swiftly to the Daṇḍaka forest; with joined palms, the charioteer consoles her, assuring her that Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa dwell serenely in the woods.

item.title: ०६१ कौसल्याकृतदशरथनिन्दा
item.description:
वाचनम्
सर्वाष् टीकाः
Murali Krishnamurthy Kopalle Murthy - Intro

Book II : Ayodhya Kanda - Book Of Ayodhya

Kausalya, while weeping, rebukes Dasaratha for his evil act of sending Rama to exile. She explains various difficulties being faced by Rama, Lakshmana and Seetha in their forest-life. She says that even if Rama returns to Ayodhya in the fifteenth year, he may not accept the kingdom since enjoyed by Bharata.

भागसूचना
  1. कौसल्याका विलापपूर्वक राजा दशरथको उपालम्भ देना

item.title: ०६२ कौसल्याकृतदशरथसान्त्वनम्
item.description:
वाचनम्
सर्वाष् टीकाः
Murali Krishnamurthy Kopalle Murthy - Intro

Book II : Ayodhya Kanda - Book Of Ayodhya

After hearing harsh words from Kausalya, king Dasaratha loses consciousness and restores it after a long time. Afterwards, Kausalya repents for her mistake of speaking such crude words and consoles the king with her reconciliatory words. Overcome by grief, Dasaratha fell into the grip, Dasaratha fell into the grip of slumber as the night prevailed.

भागसूचना
  1. दुःखी हुए राजा दशरथका कौसल्याको हाथ जोड़कर मनाना और कौसल्याका उनके चरणोंमें पड़कर क्षमा माँगना

item.title: ०६३ दशरथेन पूर्वकृतबालवधकथनम्
item.description:
वाचनम्
सर्वाष् टीकाः
Murali Krishnamurthy Kopalle Murthy - Intro

Book II : Ayodhya Kanda - Book Of Ayodhya

Dasaratha woke up with anxious thoughts. Recalling his earlier sin, he starts recounting the story of a young ascetic to Kausalya. He says that while he was Prince Regent of Ayodhya, he went out for hunting in a forest one day and heard the sound of a hermit-boy filling his pitcher with water by suberging it into Sarayu River. Mistaking the gurgling sound for trumpeting of an elephant the prince hit the boy with an arrow, which went deep into the body and mortally wounded him. On approaching the victim, he discovered the fatal blunder and tendered his heart felt apologies to the hermit boy, who asked him to extract the arrow from his body and inform his parents. The boy died soon after the arrow was drawn out from the body.

भागसूचना
  1. राजा दशरथका शोक और उनका कौसल्यासे अपने द्वारा मुनिकुमारके मारे जानेका प्रसङ्ग सुनाना

item.title: ०६४ दशरथमृतिः
item.description:
वाचनम्
सर्वाष् टीकाः
Murali Krishnamurthy Kopalle Murthy - Intro

Book II : Ayodhya Kanda - Book Of Ayodhya

King Dasaratha continued to narrate to Kausalya how he went to the aged parents of the deceased sage and informed about the death of their son and its cause, how he escorted them to their son to the river where he was lying dead, how embracing the boy they wept and offered libations of water to his spirit, how invested with an ethereal body, the spirit ascended to heaven while consoling the aged couple and finally how, having cursed the king that he too would die of agony caused by the separation from his son, the aged couple gave up their lives. Having thus narrated the story of his getting the curse long back and loudly weeping, king Dasaratha dies of grief.

भागसूचना
  1. राजा दशरथका अपने द्वारा मुनिकुमारके वधसे दुःखी हुए उनके माता-पिताके विलाप और उनके दिये हुए शापका प्रसंग सुनाकर कौसल्याके समीप रोते-बिलखते हुए आधी रातके समय अपने प्राणोंको त्याग देना

item.title: ०६५ अन्तःपुरशोकः
item.description:
वाचनम्
सर्वाष् टीकाः
Murali Krishnamurthy Kopalle Murthy - Intro

Book II : Ayodhya Kanda - Book Of Ayodhya

At the dawn of the next day, panergysts and servants arrived at the palace to serve the king. Some women, who were empowered to go near the bed, detected the king’s death and started crying loudly. Kausalya and Sumitra suddenly woke up from their slumber and came to know of the king’s death. All the wives of Dasaratha wept miserably. The gynaecium was filled with men and women who felt bewildered with fear and restlessness; when the king met with his appointed end.

भागसूचना
  1. वन्दीजनोंका स्तुतिपाठ, राजा दशरथको दिवंगत हुआ जान उनकी रानियोंका करुण-विलाप

item.title: ०६६ राजशरीरस्य तैलकटाहे निक्षेपः
item.description:
वाचनम्
सर्वाष् टीकाः
Murali Krishnamurthy Kopalle Murthy - Intro

Book II : Ayodhya Kanda - Book Of Ayodhya

Kausalya reproaches Kaikeyi for her wrong deeds, while weeping profusely for her husband’s death. The chamberlains reverently remove Kausalya from the place of the king’s body, which they later keep in a trough filled with oil. The ministers and other functionaries return to their abodes, when the night fell in darkness.

भागसूचना
  1. राजाके लिये कौसल्याका विलाप और कैकेयीकी भर्त्सना, मन्त्रियोंका राजाके शवको तेलसे भरे हुए कड़ाहमें सुलाना, रानियोंका विलाप, पुरीकी श्रीहीनता और पुरवासियोंका शोक
